groups.title: Prisma ORM Fundamentals
groups.question: Your Remix app uses Prisma, and in development you hit 'too many connections' after a few edits. Explain the schema's role and how to create the client safely.

followUps.Prisma Schema and Data Modeling: Why must schema changes go through the Prisma schema?
followUps.PrismaClient Singleton Pattern: Why does HMR exhaust connections and how does a singleton help?

evidence.text: The schema defines both the database structure and the TypeScript types.
Changing the database directly makes them disagree.
The client is regenerated from the schema to stay in sync.

notEnough: Only saying the schema defines models.

evidence.text: Hot reloading can create a new client on each change.
Each client opens its own connections.
Storing one client on a global variable reuses it.

notEnough: Only saying you use a singleton.

groups.title: Querying with Prisma
groups.question: Your user loader returns password hashes to the client, and creating an order sometimes leaves orphaned records. Explain how you would query and write safely.

followUps.findUnique, findMany, and Select: How does select help with performance and security?
followUps.Transactions and Atomic Operations: When must you use a transaction?

evidence.text: findUnique fetches one record and findMany fetches lists.
select returns only the chosen fields.
This avoids sending sensitive fields like password hashes to the page.
Related writes, like an order and its items, must succeed or fail together.
A transaction rolls back every write if one fails.
Without it, a failure can leave half-saved data.

groups.title: SQLite in Development
groups.question: Your migrations work locally on SQLite but fail on production PostgreSQL, and someone edited the database by hand. Explain the risks and the right workflow.

followUps.SQLite Limitations and Production Parity: Why can SQLite in development cause production surprises?
followUps.Prisma Migrate and Schema Drift: What is schema drift and how do migrations prevent it?

evidence.text: SQLite has limited ALTER TABLE support and handles concurrent writes differently.
Behaviour and migrations that work in SQLite can fail in PostgreSQL.
Using the same database in development as in production avoids this.
migrate dev creates versioned SQL migration files.
Manual database edits make the real schema differ from the migrations.
Drift breaks future migrations and other environments.

groups.title: Data Access Patterns
groups.question: Your loaders contain long Prisma queries and tests fail randomly because they share a development database. Explain how you would organise data access and test data.

followUps.Repository Pattern with Remix Loaders: Why move queries out of loaders into model functions?
followUps.Seeding and Test Databases: How do seeds and separate test databases help?

evidence.text: Query logic lives in dedicated model or repository functions.
Loaders stay short and focused on the request.
Queries can be tested and reused across routes.
A seed script fills a fresh database with known data.
Tests use their own database, not the shared development one.
Tests become reliable because they start from known state.
